headline: Tim Sweeney, chief executive of the Fortnite maker Epic Games, says the company is shifting its game development heavily towards AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a major games company's stated shift to AI, confirmed by its chief executive, with no figures on jobs.
importance_line: Developers and artists at Epic and across the games industry face a workplace shift towards AI tools, which a game designer quoted by the BBC says takes away artists' jobs while Sweeney argues it will help creators build more, but no job numbers are given and Epic has not commented on the Disney delay.
summary: BBC News reports that Tim Sweeney, founder and chief executive of Epic Games, maker of Fortnite, confirmed in posts on X that the company is making a "huge pivot" towards AI in game development and is moving developers to "retool for maximum AI acceleration", saying the aim is not to do the same work with fewer people but to let developers build "more" and "better stuff". The BBC links this to an earlier Bloomberg report that Epic delayed a Disney collaboration featuring Star Wars and Marvel characters and told staff to use AI tools, with directors reportedly saying "no more hand-written code", and notes that Epic laid off more than 1,000 employees six months ago, which Sweeney then blamed on a downturn in Fortnite engagement, not AI.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Bloomberg's report is described through the BBC; Epic has not commented on the Disney delay in the text.
